note.text: A cooperative is a voluntarily formed, jointly owned and democratically controlled enterprise meeting members’ common needs. Primary cooperatives normally follow one member, one vote under the cooperative principle. Capital is needed, but a larger contribution does not by itself create proportionately more votes in that model. Membership involves responsibilities as well as benefits. A cooperative can earn a surplus; it is not defined as an organisation forbidden to trade or charge prices. Exact form and governance rules must be checked under the relevant framework.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain common member needs and distinguish democratic control from capital-based voting. Builds on: comparison of ownership, finance and control. Leads to: types of cooperative and the use of a cooperative surplus.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Fictional growers near Bamenda pool services to improve access to inputs and buyers. Members elect accountable representatives and decide through the agreed democratic process. Their purpose and governance distinguish the cooperative from a firm controlled only by the largest ordinary-share holding. Neither democratic ownership nor shared marketing guarantees a favourable harvest or price.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the members, the common service and the decision rule. Distinguish capital contribution, voting and benefit allocation: they need not use the same basis. Read the ballot conditions before counting votes and do not invent proxy rules.

questions.prompt: A fictional primary cooperative follows one member, one vote. It has {members} eligible members, of whom {absent} do not participate in this ballot. How many participating members’ votes can be cast, assuming no proxy or other special arrangements?

misconceptions.explain: That includes the absent members despite the ballot conditions.
Absence reduces participation; it does not add votes.

solution: Count participating eligible members, not the value of their contributions.
